I don’t have direct access to your host’s Docker daemon from here, so I can’t run `docker ps` myself.  
If you want to verify whether Docker is up and see what containers are currently running, open a terminal (or PowerShell) on the machine where Docker Desktop/Engine is installed and type:

```powershell
docker info   # shows overall status – look for “Server Version” etc.
```

and then

```powershell
docker ps      # lists all *running* containers
docker ps -a    # lists all containers, including stopped ones
```

The output will tell you whether the Docker service is active (`Docker version …`, `Operating System…`) and show each container’s ID, image, state, ports, etc. If those commands fail because Docker isn’t found, it means Docker isn’t installed or its executable isn’t in the PATH.
